transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
Lately, I've been having a really hard time listening when people are talking to me. It feels like I just space out, even when someone is looking right at me and speaking directly to me.
Do you also often feel restless, fidgety, or interrupt people before they finish speaking?

Yes, I do. I'm constantly fidgeting, tapping my hands or feet, and I find it really hard to just sit still. I also have a tough time waiting my turn, so I often end up interrupting people or speaking out of turn.
Did these attention and restlessness symptoms start in childhood, before age 12, and have they been present in more than one setting like school, work, and home?

Yes, absolutely, these struggles definitely started back in elementary school, well before I turned 12. They have always affected me in different areas of my life, from trying to get chores done at home to managing my daily tasks at work.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation). The new information supports this diagnosis: symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are both present, they began before age 12, and they occur across multiple settings (home and work). No evidence was introduced to suggest an alternative diagnosis, so the candidate list remains the same.

inference_history.note: No previous candidates were provided. Based on the initial complaint of frequently spacing out and difficulty listening even when directly addressed, an inattentive ADHD presentation is most likely. However, concentration problems can also occur with depression or anxiety, so those remain in the differential. Hyperactive/impulsive ADHD, psychotic disorders, bipolar disorders, and eating/trauma-related disorders are not suggested by the current history.
